meta.pageTitle: GATE CSE Theory of Computation Previous Year Questions - Solved PYQs

questions.text:
Consider the following sets:

S1: Set of all recursively enumerable languages over the alphabet {0, 1}.
S2: Set of all syntactically valid C programs.
S3: Set of all languages over the alphabet {0, 1}.
S4: Set of all non-regular languages over the alphabet {0, 1}.

Which of the above sets are uncountable?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- S1: every RE language has a TM, and TMs can be listed [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] countable.
- S2: C programs are finite strings [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] countable.
- S3: all languages = the power set of [latex]\{0,1\}^*[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] uncountable.
- S4: S3 minus the countably many regular languages is still uncountable.

Answer: S3 and S4

questions.text: Which one of the following languages over [latex]\Sigma =\{a,b\}[/latex] is NOT context-free?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- [latex]ww^R[/latex]: even palindromes [latex]\text{---}[/latex] CFL.
- [latex]wa^nb^nw^R[/latex]: nested matching (w with [latex]w^R[/latex] outside, a's with b's inside) [latex]\text{---}[/latex] CFL.
- [latex]\{a^nb^i\mid i\in\{n,3n,5n\}\}[/latex]: union of three CFLs [latex]\text{---}[/latex] CFL.
- [latex]wa^nw^Rb^n[/latex]: the w-[latex]w^R[/latex] match and the a-b match cross each other, which one stack cannot handle [latex]\text{---}[/latex] not CFL.

Answer: [latex]\{wa^nw^Rb^n\}[/latex]

questions.text:
For [latex]\Sigma =\{a,b\}[/latex], let us consider the regular language
[latex]L=\{x|x=a^{2+3k} \; or \; x=b^{10+12k}, k\geq 0\}[/latex].
Which one of the following can be a pumping length (the constant guaranteed by the pumping lemma) for L?
questions.solution:
p must be larger than any string that cannot be pumped.
- [latex]b^{10}[/latex] cannot be pumped: removing any part gives fewer than 10 b's, which is not in L. So p must be at least 11 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 3, 5, 9 fail.
- With p = 24: every b-string of length [latex]\ge24[/latex] (34, 46, [latex]\ldots[/latex]) can pump [latex]y=b^{12}[/latex] inside the first 24 symbols, and every a-string can pump [latex]y=aaa[/latex].

Answer: 24

questions.text: If L is a regular language over [latex]\Sigma =\{a,b\}[/latex], which one of the following languages is NOT regular ?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- [latex]L\cdot L^R[/latex]: regular languages are closed under reversal and concatenation [latex]\text{---}[/latex] regular.
- Prefix(L), Suffix(L): closed operations on regular languages [latex]\text{---}[/latex] regular.
- [latex]\{ww^R\mid w\in L\}[/latex]: take [latex]L=\Sigma^*[/latex]; this gives even-length palindromes, which are not regular.

Answer: [latex]\{ww^R\mid w\in L\}[/latex]

questions.text: A CFG (Context Free Grammar) is said to be in Chomsky Normal Form (CNF), if all the productions are of the form [latex]\mathrm{A} \rightarrow \mathrm{BC}[/latex] or [latex]\mathrm{A} \rightarrow \mathrm{a}[/latex]. Let G be a CFG in CNF. To derive a string of terminals of length x, the number of products to be used is:
questions.solution:
In CNF, [latex]A\rightarrow BC[/latex] grows the number of symbols by 1, so x [latex]-[/latex] 1 such steps build x variables; then x steps of [latex]A\rightarrow a[/latex] turn them into terminals.

Total = (x [latex]-[/latex] 1) + x = 2x [latex]-[/latex] 1

Answer: 2x-1
